question: Should OpenClaw publish `api.registerReadinessCriterion` and `gateway.readiness` selection as a supported V1 plugin and operator compatibility contract?
rationale: This choice determines a durable external SDK and configuration surface, including what plugins may report and what operators may rely on; source inspection cannot substitute for maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Approve the bounded V1 contract
options.body: Accept the public callback and selector identifiers, then require exact-head proof that unconfigured deployments retain legacy readiness and selected required criteria fail and recover predictably.

options.title: Land core-only readiness later
options.body: Defer public plugin registration while retaining only core-owned observations behind a narrower approved implementation.

options.title: Defer the readiness program
options.body: Decline the V1 contract for now and avoid adding the config and plugin SDK surface until a future product decision sponsors it.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the public callback and selector identifiers, then require exact-head proof that unconfigured deployments retain legacy readiness and selected required criteria fail and recover predictably.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the interconnected readiness proposal stack and can provide the technical contract details while a repository decision-maker confirms product direction.
